text:
Mason McTavish is in his first season with the Blues after 304 games in Anaheim, and the early returns are a fair picture of who he is. Nine goals in 26 games, a power-play breakaway goal against New Jersey and a shootout move against Dallas that the Blues' own video called insane. The scoring touch is real: his own chances run at 1.41 expected goals per 60 minutes, up from 1.22 with the Ducks, and nine goals on 9.6 expected is right on the number.

The minutes are the question. He is playing 15:47 a night overall but only about 15 over the last ten games, with four nights at 13 minutes or less, and three points in that stretch. Evolving-Hockey's read from last season explains why coaches hesitate: he drives offense, but opponents got more with him on the ice than with almost any forward.

St. Louis has 51% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there, a couple of points better than without him, and the Blues have finished below their chances around him. If his ice time climbs, the scoring is there to follow.
